duplicate_analysis.conclusion: LEGITIMATE association-format repetition: each disease repeats a small set of canonical symptom vectors many times to reach 121 rows class (5-10 unique vectors per disease, 111-116 repeat rows each). Every repeated symptom vector maps to exactly ONE disease (0 contradictions). Repeated rows are therefore NOT independent patient observations; the underlying information is a disease->symptom association table. No accidental duplication or polysemy is evidenced.
duplicate_analysis.interpretation: None of the repeated rows are independent patient samples a priori; they are structured repeats of disease->symptom association vectors.

contradiction_analysis.note: Contradictions documented for Phase 7I; not resolved by guessing in this phase.

separability.note: Cosines are class-mean profile similarities (structural geometry), NOT clinical validity. Deduplication does not materially change separability.

leakage.description: Repeated rows are exact repeats of the same symptom vector. Random row-level train/test splitting places identical vectors on BOTH sides -> identical information appears in train and test -> overly optimistic evaluation.

recommended_strategy.split: GROUPED split by unique symptom vector (LeaveOneVectorOut / GroupKFold-like): assign each unique vector to exactly one fold; NEVER split identical vectors across folds. With 5-10 vectors per class, use repeated grouped CV (e.g., 5-fold grouped, repeated 10x) and report macro metrics + per-class support. Because classes have only 5-10 association vectors, small-dataset uncertainty is expected and must be reported.
recommended_strategy.avoid: Random row-level split on the 4,961-row file (would leak identical vectors), and any split that lets a vector appear in both train and test.
recommended_strategy.evaluation_limitations: 41 classes but only 304 total association vectors -> evaluation is inherently small-sample; treat results as exploratory, not clinical.
